title: Sep 26 Results + Sep 27 Preview: Nine Wins Never Gets Old
summary: 69.2% accuracy on Friday's slate - now eyeing Mets-Nationals for Saturday's top play

content.value:
## Another Solid Day in the Books

You know, after covering this game for as long as I have, a 9-4 day still brings a smile. That's 69.2% accuracy when it matters most - late September baseball where every pitch carries weight. We've seen plenty of these stretched runs before, and the model continues to find edges where others see coin flips.

## The Hits That Mattered

The Dodgers took care of business against the Giants at 63% confidence - that's the kind of solid chalk play that builds a winning day. Tampa Bay came through at 61% against the Phillies, and frankly, I've seen the Rays pull off that exact game a hundred times. The Braves handled Miami, the Brewers got past St. Louis, and Texas surprised some folks in Minnesota.

The misses? Well, the Nationals got us early, the Blue Jays couldn't capitalize, the Royals had other plans, and Boston stumbled at home. That's baseball in September - even the 50-50 calls can sting when they don't break your way.

## Tomorrow's Top Pick Preview

Here's the thing about the Mets and Nationals - we just saw this matchup yesterday, and now we're flipping the script. Sean Manaea gets the ball for New York against DJ Herz, and the model likes the Mets at 53%. It's not a screaming play, but I've learned over the years that September divisional rematches often come down to who adjusted better overnight.

Manaea has been steady when the Mets need him to be, and Herz is still finding his way at this level. Nothing flashy here - just a veteran pitcher with something to prove against a young arm in a ballpark that's seen its share of surprising outcomes.

content.title: ⭐ Saturday's Top Pick - Sep 27
content.sub: Pick: Mets (53%) • Manaea vs Herz • Trust the veteran arm

content.value:
## The Veteran's Take

I've covered enough late-season series to know that momentum matters, but so does matchup quality. The Mets lost Friday's opener, and typically that lights a fire. Manaea knows what's at stake, and that 53% edge might not look like much on paper, but in this context? I'll take the experienced left-hander getting one more chance to silence the home crowd.

See you Saturday with the results. Stay sharp out there.
